/dev0/auxins/0/averaging.Description: Defines the number of samples on the input to average as a power of two. Possible values are in the range [0, 16]. A value of 0 corresponds to the sampling rate of the auxiliary input's ADC.

/dev0/auxins/0/sample.Description: Voltage measured at the Auxiliary Input after averaging. The data rate depends on the averaging value. Note, if the instrument has demodulator functionality, the auxiliary input values are available as fields in a demodulator sample and are aligned by timestamp with the demodulator output.

/dev0/auxins/0/values/0.Description: Voltage measured at the Auxiliary Input after averaging. The value of this node is updated at a low rate (50 Hz); the streaming node auxins/n/sample is updated at a high rate defined by the averaging.

/dev0/auxouts/0/demodselect.Description: Select the channel number of the selected signal source.

/dev0/auxouts/0/limitlower.Description: Lower limit for the signal at the Auxiliary Output. A smaller value will be clipped.

/dev0/auxouts/0/limitupper.Description: Upper limit for the signal at the Auxiliary Output. A larger value will be clipped.

/dev0/auxouts/0/max.Description: Indicates the maximum normalized voltage generated on this channel. It can be between -1 and 1. To prevent signal clipping and overvoltage, it is advised to keep it between -0.9 and 0.9.

/dev0/auxouts/0/min.Description: Indicates the minimum normalized voltage generated on this channel. It can be between -1 and 1. To prevent signal clipping and overvoltage, it is advised to keep it between -0.9 and 0.9.

/dev0/auxouts/0/offset.Description: Add the specified offset voltage to the signal after scaling. Auxiliary Output Value = (Signal+Preoffset)*Scale + Offset

/dev0/auxouts/0/outputselect.Description: Select the signal source to be represented on the Auxiliary Output.

Options.-1: "manual": Select Manual as the output option.
Options.0: "demod_x": Select Demod X as the output option.
Options.1: "demod_y": Select Demod Y as the output option.
Options.2: "demod_r": Select Demod R as the output option.
Options.3: "demod_theta": Select Demod Theta as the output option.
Options.5: "pid", "pid_out": Select PID Out as the output option.
Options.6: "boxcar": Select Boxcar as the output option.
Options.9: "pid_shift": Select PID Shift as the output option.
Options.10: "pid_error": Select PID Error as the output option.
Options.11: "tu_filtered": Select TU Filtered Value as the output option.
Options.13: "tu_output": Select TU Output Value as the output option.

/dev0/auxouts/0/preoffset.Description: Add a pre-offset to the signal before scaling is applied. Auxiliary Output Value = (Signal+Preoffset)*Scale + Offset

/dev0/auxouts/0/scale.Description: Multiplication factor to scale the signal. Auxiliary Output Value = (Signal+Preoffset)*Scale + Offset

Options.0: "off": Switch off the Tip Protect unit.
Options.1: "on": Switch on the Tip Protect unit.

/dev0/auxouts/0/tipprotect/polarity.Description: Select the active level of Source signal.

Options.0: "low": Active when the source signal is at low level.
Options.1: "high": Active when the source signal is at high level.

/dev0/auxouts/0/tipprotect/source.Description: Select the input source for Tip Protect.

Options.0: "tu_output0": Select Threshold Unit 1 as the source signal.
Options.1: "tu_output1": Select Threshold Unit 2 as the source signal.
Options.2: "tu_output2": Select Threshold Unit 3 as the source signal.
Options.3: "tu_output3": Select Threshold Unit 4 as the source signal.

/dev0/auxouts/0/tipprotect/value.Description: Signal value written to the Aux Output port when Tip Protect is active. The value overwrites Aux Output Internal value and the Lower and Upper Limits.

/dev0/auxouts/0/value.Description: Voltage present on the Auxiliary Output. Auxiliary Output Value = (Signal+Preoffset)*Scale + Offset

/dev0/boxcars/0/averagerbandwidth.Description: The 3 dB signal bandwidth of the Boxcar Averager is determined by the oscillation frequency and the Number of Averaging Periods set. Note: internally the boxcar signal is sampled at a rate of 14 MSa/s and the signal bandwidth of the auxiliary output is 7 MHz.

/dev0/boxcars/0/baseline/windowstart.Description: Boxcar baseline suppression gate opening start in degrees based on one oscillator frequency period equals 360 degrees.

/dev0/boxcars/0/decimation.Description: Indicates, in powers of 2, the number of averager outputs sent to the PC while Averaging Periods Boxcar integrations are obtained. Positive integer values indicate oversampling. Negative integer values indicate undersampling. Examples for oversampling values: 0 : 2^0 = 1 averager output is sent to the PC during Averaging Periods Boxcar integrations. 2 : 2^2 = 4 averager outputs are sent to the PC during Averaging Periods Boxcar integrations. -1 : 2^-1 = 0.5, only every other Averaging Periods Boxcar integrations an averager output is sent to the PC.

/dev0/boxcars/0/fifooverflow.Description: Data lost during streaming to PC. Sticky flag cleared by restarting the boxcar.

/dev0/boxcars/0/inputselect.Description: Select Signal Input used for the boxcar analysis.

/dev0/boxcars/0/limitrate.Description: Rate Limit for Boxcar output data sent to PC. This value does not affect the Aux Output for which the effective rate is given by min(14 MSa/s , Frequency / max(1, Averaging Periods/512)).

/dev0/boxcars/0/oscselect.Description: Selection of the oscillator used for the boxcar analysis.

/dev0/boxcars/0/periodoverflowevents.Description: The boxcar averaging gate opening width is more than one cycle of the signal and should be reduced.

/dev0/boxcars/0/rate.Description: Current data transfer rate to the PC given by min(14 MSa/s , Frequency / max(1, Averaging Periods/512)). This value is read-only.

/dev0/boxcars/0/sample.Description: Streaming node containing the output data of the boxcar.

/dev0/boxcars/0/windowsize.Description: Boxcar averaging gate opening width in seconds. It can be converted to phase assuming 360 equals to a full period of the driving oscillator.

/dev0/boxcars/0/windowstart.Description: Boxcar averaging gate opening start in degrees. It can be converted to time assuming 360 equals to a full period of the driving oscillator.

/dev0/clockbase.Description: Returns the internal clock frequency of the device.

/dev0/currins/0/autorange.Description: Automatic adjustment of the Range to approximately two times the maximum current input amplitude.

/dev0/currins/0/float.Description: Switches the input between floating (ON) and connected grounds (OFF). This setting applies both to the voltage and the current input. It is recommended to discharge the test device before connecting or to enable this setting only after the signal source has been connected to the Signal Input in grounded mode.

/dev0/currins/0/max.Description: Indicates the maximum normalized current measured on this channel. It can be between -1 and 1. To prevent signal clipping and overcurrent, it is advised to keep it between -0.9 and 0.9.

/dev0/currins/0/min.Description: Indicates the minimum normalized current measured on this channel. It can be between -1 and 1. To prevent signal clipping and overcurrent, it is advised to keep it between -0.9 and 0.9.

/dev0/currins/0/range.Description: Defines the gain of the current input amplifier. The range should exceed the incoming signal by roughly a factor of two including a potential DC offset. The instrument selects the next higher available range relative to a value inserted by the user. A suitable choice of this setting optimizes the accuracy and signal-to-noise ratio by ensuring that the full dynamic range of the input ADC is used.

/dev0/currins/0/rangestep/trigger.Description: Switches to the next appropriate input range such that the range fits best with the measured input current.

/dev0/currins/0/scaling.Description: Applies the given scale factor to the current input.

/dev0/demods/0/adcselect.Description: Selects the input signal for the demodulator.

Options.174: "demod_constant_input": Demodulate a constant input. This results in a sine wave of the frequency specified by the demodulator's oscillator with an amplitude of 1 (at lower frequencies; higher frequencies will be attenuated). The maximum possible frequency is limited by the demodulator sampling rate and bandwidth; use demodulator order 1 for the least attenuation in demodulator output. This signal may be used with the auxiliary outputs, PID and Threshold Unit for advanced measurement and control tasks. When the demodulator output is written to an auxiliary output, the resulting signal can also be used as a second output channel (for low frequencies).

/dev0/demods/0/enable.Description: Enables the data acquisition for the corresponding demodulator. Note: increasing number of active demodulators increases load on the physical connection to the host computer.

/dev0/demods/0/freq.Description: Indicates the frequency used for demodulation and for output generation. The demodulation frequency is calculated as oscillator frequency times the harmonic factor. When the MOD option is used linear combinations of oscillator frequencies including the harmonic factors define the sideband frequencies.

/dev0/demods/0/harmonic.Description: Multiplies the selected oscillator's frequency by an integer. If the demodulator is used as a phase detector in external reference mode (PLL), the effect is that the internal oscillator locks to the external frequency divided by the integer factor.

/dev0/demods/0/order.Description: Selects the filter roll off between 6 dB/oct and 48 dB/oct.

/dev0/demods/0/oscselect.Description: Assignes an oscillator to the demodulator. Number of available oscillators depends on the installed options.

/dev0/demods/0/phaseadjust.Description: Adjust the demodulator phase automatically in order to read 0 degrees.

/dev0/demods/0/phaseshift.Description: Applies phase shift to the reference input of the demodulator.

/dev0/demods/0/rate.Description: Defines the demodulator sampling rate, the number of samples that are sent to the host computer per second. A rate of about 7-10 higher as compared to the filter bandwidth usually provides sufficient aliasing suppression. This is also the rate of data received by LabOne Data Server and saved to the computer hard disk. This setting has no impact on the sample rate on the auxiliary outputs connectors. Note: the value inserted by the user may be approximated to the nearest value supported by the instrument.

/dev0/demods/0/sample.Description: Contains streamed demodulator samples with sample interval defined by the demodulator data rate.

/dev0/demods/0/sinc.Description: Enables the sinc filter. When the filter bandwidth is comparable to or larger than the demodulation frequency, the demodulator output may contain frequency components at the frequency of demodulation and its higher harmonics. The sinc is an additional filter that attenuates these unwanted components in the demodulator output.

/dev0/demods/0/timeconstant.Description: Sets the integration time constant or in other words, the cutoff frequency of the demodulator low pass filter.

/dev0/demods/0/trigger.Description: Selects the acquisition mode (i.e. triggering) of the demodulator.

Options.0: "continuous": Continuous: demodulator data is continuously streamed to the host computer.
Options.3: "trigin0_both", "trigger_input0_both": Trigger Input 1: triggering on both rising and falling edge.
Options.5: "trigin0or1_rising", "trigger_input0or1_rising": Trigger Input 1 or 2: rising edge triggered on either input.
Options.10: "trigin0or1_falling", "trigger_input0or1_falling": Trigger Input 1 or 2: falling edge triggered on either input.
Options.12: "trigin1_both", "trigger_input1_both": Trigger Input 2: triggering on both rising and falling edge.
Options.15: "trigin0or1_both", "trigger_input0or1_both": Trigger Input 1 or 2: triggering on both rising and falling edge or either trigger input.
Options.16: "trigin0_low", "trigger_input0_low": Trigger Input 1: demodulator data is streamed to the host computer when the level is low (TTL).
Options.32: "trigin0_high", "trigger_input0_high": Trigger Input 1 for MF: demodulator data is streamed to the host computer when the level is high (TTL).
Options.64: "trigin1_low", "trigger_input1_low": Trigger Input 2: demodulator data is streamed to the host computer when the level is low (TTL).
Options.80: "trigin0or1_low", "trigger_input0or1_low": Trigger Input 1 or 2: demodulator data is streamed to the host computer when either level is low (TTL).
Options.128: "trigin1_high", "trigger_input1_high": Trigger Input 2: demodulator data is streamed to the host computer when the level is high (TTL).
Options.160: "trigin0or1_high", "trigger_input0or1_high": Trigger Input 1 or 2: demodulator data is streamed to the host computer when either level is high (TTL).

/dev0/dios/0/auxdrive.Description: Not used. Reserved for future use.

/dev0/dios/0/decimation.Description: Sets the decimation factor for DIO data streamed to the host computer.

/dev0/dios/0/drive.Description: When on (1), the corresponding 8-bit bus is in output mode. When off (0), it is in input mode. Bit 0 corresponds to the least significant byte. For example, the value 1 drives the least significant byte, the value 8 drives the most significant byte.

/dev0/dios/0/extclk.Description: Select DIO internal or external clocking.

Options.0: "internal": The DIO is internally clocked with a fixed frequency of 60 MHz.
Options.1: "external": The DIO is externally clocked with a clock signal connected to DIO Pin 68. The available range is from 1 Hz up to the internal clock frequency.

/dev0/dios/0/input.Description: Gives the value of the DIO input for those bytes where drive is disabled.

Options.0: "manual": Enables manual control of the DIO output bits.
Options.3: "threshold_unit": Enables setting of DIO output values by the threshold unit.

/dev0/dios/0/output.Description: Sets the value of the DIO output for those bytes where 'drive' is enabled.

/dev0/extrefs/0/adcselect.Description: Indicates the input signal selection for the selected demodulator.

Options.0: "sigin0", "signal_input0": Signal Input 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.1: "currin0", "current_input0": Current Input 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.2: "trigin0", "trigger_input0": Trigger Input 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.3: "trigin1", "trigger_input1": Trigger Input 2 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.4: "auxout0", "auxiliary_output0": Auxiliary Output 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.5: "auxout1", "auxiliary_output1": Auxiliary Output 2 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.6: "auxout2", "auxiliary_output2": Auxiliary Output 3 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.7: "auxout3", "auxiliary_output3": Auxiliary Output 4 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.8: "auxin0", "auxiliary_input0": Auxiliary Input 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.9: "auxin1", "auxiliary_input1": Auxiliary Input 2 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.174: "demod_constant_input": Constant is connected to the corresponding demodulator. This results in a sine wave of the frequency specified by the demodulator's oscillator with an amplitude of 1 or lower, depending on frequency and filter settings.

/dev0/extrefs/0/automode.Description: This defines the type of automatic adaptation of parameters in the PID used for Ext Ref.

Options.2: "low_bandwidth", "pid_coeffs_filter_low_bw": The PID coefficients, the filter bandwidth and the output limits are automatically set using a low bandwidth.
Options.3: "high_bandwidth", "pid_coeffs_filter_high_bw": The PID coefficients, the filter bandwidth and the output limits are automatically set using a high bandwidth.
Options.4: "all", "pid_coeffs_filter_auto_bw": The PID coefficient, the filter bandwidth and the output limits are dynamically adapted.

/dev0/extrefs/0/demodselect.Description: Indicates the demodulator connected to the extref channel.

/dev0/extrefs/0/locked.Description: Indicates whether the external reference is locked.

/dev0/extrefs/0/oscselect.Description: Indicates which oscillator is being locked to the external reference.

/dev0/features/code.Description: Node providing a mechanism to write feature codes.

/dev0/imps/0/ac.Description: Defines the input coupling for the Signal Inputs. AC coupling inserts a high-pass filter.

/dev0/imps/0/auto/bw.Description: Enable automatic bandwidth control. If enabled the optimum bandwidth is calculated based on the frequency and measurement data.

Options.0: Manual: In manual mode the current and voltage input ranges are adjusted manually and separately. Use this mode with care as overload will result in inaccurate impedance results.
Options.1: Auto: Dynamically adjust the input range according to the measured input signal strength. This optimizes the dynamic range and precision of impedance measurements.
Options.2: Zone: This ranging option allows you to manually set the switching frequency limits for all eight current input ranges.

/dev0/imps/0/auto/output.Description: If enabled, the drive voltage amplitude is controlled by the device. If disabled it can be set manually.

/dev0/imps/0/auto/suppress.Description: Indicates disabled periodic auto range control. A running sweeper module takes over the range control and thus disables the periodic range checks.

/dev0/imps/0/bias/value.Description: DC bias voltage applied across the device under test. Both positive and negative bias voltages are supported. In a 4-terminal measurement, the bias voltage is limited by the maximum common voltage input range of the device. In a 2-terminal measurement, the bias voltage can be larger because the voltage inputs are not connected.

/dev0/imps/0/calib/internal/active.Description: Indicates if the internal calibration is applied to the measurement data.

/dev0/imps/0/calib/internal/enable.Description: Enables the internal calibration. This ensures that the input range gains match over the full frequency range. With enabled internal calibration the device fulfills the impedance accuracy specification. The internal calibration is a prerequisite to apply a user compensation.

/dev0/imps/0/calib/internal/smooth.Description: Enables smoothing of the internal calibration data. This results in lower noise in the measured data.

/dev0/imps/0/calib/user/active.Description: Indicates that a valid user compensation is active. If active the impedance data streams deliver amplitude and phase corrected data based on the impedance user compensation.

/dev0/imps/0/calib/user/enable.Description: Enables the user compensation of the impedance data. The user compensation is correcting parasitics and delays caused by the external setup. The user compensation is applied on top of the internal impedance calibration.

/dev0/imps/0/calib/user/smooth.Description: Enables smoothing of the compensation data. This results in lower noise in the measured data.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/compensation/ena.Description: Enables the indication of strong compensation in the plots. A strong compensation diminishes the measurement accuracy of the parameter.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/compensation/rat.Description: Strength of the compensation that will trigger the strong compensation warning.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/enable.Description: Enables/disables all confidence indicators to check the reliability of the measured data. To enable individual indicators, open the advanced tab.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/freqlimit/enable.Description: Enables the frequency limit detection based on the used current input range. Only relevant when Range Control is set to Manual.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/lowdut2t/enable.Description: Enables a warning when meassuring a low impedance (100k) with a 2 point contact.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/lowdut2t/ratio.Description: When measuring with 2 point contacts, too low impedance of DUT will trigger the Low DUT 2T warning.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/oneperiod/enable.Description: Enables the detection of unreliable data points where data sample loss leads to an invalid one-period average. Try reducing the data transfer rate.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/opendetect/enabl.Description: Enables the open terminal detection for 4-terminal measurements.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/opendetect/ratio.Description: Open terminal detection ratio. An open terminal is reported if the excitation calculated from current and voltage drop differs more than the specified factor from the driving voltage.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/overflow/enable.Description: Enables the overload detection for current and voltage.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/qfactor/enable.Description: Enables the detection of negative Q or D factors. Negative Q or D factors mean the measured impedance does not correspond to the chosen Representation. This can be due to an erroneous compensation, a bad choice of the Representation, or noise.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/suppression/enab.Description: The Suppression Confidence Indicator indicates if one of the two parameters of a circuit representation cannot be calculated reliably from the measured impedance. This is the case if a small variation in one (dominant) representation parameter creates a strong variation of the other (suppressed) representation parameter. Such an error amplification indicates that the measurement of the secondary parameter is unreliable.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/suppression/rati.Description: Error amplification limit for which a secondary parameter is marked unreliable. Larger gain values mean larger warning tolerances. A gain value between 10 and 100 is best.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/underflow/enable.Description: Enables the underflow detection for current and voltage.

/dev0/imps/0/confidence/underflow/ratio.Description: The underflow condition is met if the measured amplitude is lower than the specified ratio relative to full scale.

/dev0/imps/0/current/inputselect.Description: Select the current input used for two- and four-terminal impedance measurements.

/dev0/imps/0/current/invert.Description: If enabled, the current input signal is inverted. This is useful to switch the polarity of an input signal which can be caused by additional current amplifiers.

/dev0/imps/0/current/pid/enable.Description: If enabled, the PID value is used for the impedance calculation instead of the measured value at the current input.

/dev0/imps/0/current/range.Description: Input current range used for the impedance measurement. Small current input ranges have a reduced bandwidth. In the Range Control modes 'Auto' and 'Impedance', the current range is switched automatically to a higher range if the frequency is too high.

/dev0/imps/0/current/scaling.Description: The scaling factor will be applied to the current measurement done with an Aux In input.

/dev0/imps/0/demod/harmonic.Description: Multiplies the demodulator's reference frequency with the integer factor defined by this field.

/dev0/imps/0/demod/order.Description: Selects the filter roll off between 6 dB/oct and 48 dB/oct of the current demodulator.

/dev0/imps/0/demod/oscselect.Description: Oscillator used to generate the frequency of the excitation voltage on the Hcur (+V) connector.

/dev0/imps/0/demod/rate.Description: Impedance data streaming rate. The same data rate is applied to the demodulators that are used for the impedance measurement.

/dev0/imps/0/demod/timeconstant.Description: Defines low pass filter time constant.

/dev0/imps/0/discard/enable.Description: Discarding impedance samples outside the indicated range.

/dev0/imps/0/discard/limitlower.Description: Threshold for abs(Z) below which the impedance samples are discarded.

/dev0/imps/0/discard/limitupper.Description: Threshold for abs(Z) above which the impedance samples are discarded.

/dev0/imps/0/enable.Description: Enable impedance calculation for demodulator data.

/dev0/imps/0/freq.Description: Frequency control for the oscillator used for impedance measurement.

/dev0/imps/0/interpolation.Description: Select the interpolation method of the compensation data. The interpolation method is particularly important if the derivative changes strongly e.g at cut-off frequencies.

Options.0: "linear": Linear: The linear interpolation is fastest but may create compensation errors in between the frequency points used for compensation.
Options.1: "pchip": Piecewise Cubic Hermite (PCHIP): The piecewise cubic Hermite interpolation will result in very accurate results but requires more calculation power.

/dev0/imps/0/maxbandwidth.Description: Limit of the maximum bandwidth used on the demodulator filter. Values above 1 kHz can heavily diminish measurement accuracy in the high-frequency region where the amplitude is no more constant over frequency.

Options.0: 4 Terminal: This method uses the current and the voltage drop across the DUT to calculate the DUT impedance. This method results in very accurate measurements as influences of series resistors on the output and current input are excluded.
Options.1: 2 Terminal: This method uses the driving voltage and the measured current to calculate the DUT impedance. The 2 Terminal method can be beneficial when measuring very high impedance where the parasitics of the voltage measurement are limiting the frequency range.

/dev0/imps/0/model.Description: Representation of the complex impedance value Z by two real values accessible as Parameter 1 and Parameter 2 on all user interface displays.

Options.0: "r_c_parallel": Rp || Cp: Impedance value Z is represented by a resistive element Rp in parallel with a capacitive element Cp.
Options.1: "r_c_series": Rs + Cs: Impedance value Z is represented by a resistive element Rs in series with a capacitive element Cs.
Options.2: "r_l_series": Rs + Ls: Impedance value Z is represented by a resistive element Rs in series with an inductive element Ls.
Options.3: "g_b_parallel", "admittance": G B: Impedance value Z is represented by conductance G = Real(Y) and Susceptance B = Imag(Y) of the admittance Y = 1/Z.
Options.4: "d_c_series": D Cs: Impedance value Z is represented by a dissipation factor D = -Real(Z)/Imag(Z) (loss tangent) and a series capacitive element.
Options.5: "q_c_series": Q Cs: Impedance value Z is represented by a quality factor Q = -Imag(Z)/Real(Z) and a series capacitive element.
Options.6: "d_l_series": D Ls: Impedance value Z is represented by a dissipation factor D = Real(Z)/Imag(Z) (loss tangent) and a series inductive element.
Options.7: "q_l_series": Q Ls: Impedance value Z is represented by a quality factor Q = Imag(Z)/Real(Z) and a series inductive element.
Options.8: "r_l_parallel": Rp || Lp: Impedance value Z is represented by a resistive element Rp in parallel with an inductive element Lp.
Options.9: "d_c_parallel": D Cp: Impedance value Z is represented by a dissipation factor D = Real(Z)/Imag(Z) (loss tangent) and a parallel capacitive element Cp.
Options.10: "dielectric": Dielectic: Impedance value Z is represented by an equivalent dieletric material with a complex permittivity.

/dev0/imps/0/mut/area.Description: The area of the MUT. Only relevant when using the dielectric model.

/dev0/imps/0/mut/thickness.Description: The thickness of the MUT. Only relevant when using the dielectric model.

/dev0/imps/0/omegasuppression.Description: Suppression of the omega and 2-omega components. Small omega suppression can diminish measurements of very low or high impedance because the DC component can become dominant. Large omega suppression will have a significant impact on sweep time especially for low filter orders.

/dev0/imps/0/oneperiod/active.Description: Enables one-period averaging for low frequency impedance measurements. The LED is green when active.

/dev0/imps/0/oneperiod/enable.Description: Enables one-period averaging for low frequency impedance measurements. The LED is green when active.

/dev0/imps/0/output/amplitude.Description: Drive amplitude on the Signal Output.

/dev0/imps/0/output/demod.Description: Demodulator unit used to generate the excitation voltage on the Signal Output.

/dev0/imps/0/output/on.Description: Main switch for the Signal Output corresponding to the blue LED indicator on the instrument front panel.

/dev0/imps/0/output/select.Description: Selects the output channel that the excitation voltage drives.

/dev0/imps/0/sample.Description: Streaming node containing the impedance measurement sample data.

/dev0/imps/0/voltage/demodselect.Description: Demodulator used for voltage measurement in case of a four-terminal impedance measurement.

/dev0/imps/0/voltage/inputselect.Description: Select the voltage input used for a four-terminal impedance measurement.

/dev0/imps/0/voltage/invert.Description: If enabled, the voltage input signal is inverted.

/dev0/imps/0/voltage/range.Description: Input voltage range for the impedance measurement.

/dev0/imps/0/voltage/scaling.Description: The scaling factor will be applied to the voltage meaurement done with an Aux In input.

/dev0/mods/0/carrier/harmonic.Description: Set the harmonic of the carrier frequency. 1 = Fundamental

/dev0/mods/0/carrier/inputselect.Description: Select Signal Input for the carrier demodulation

Options.174: "demod_constant_input": Demodulate a constant input. This results in a sine wave of the frequency specified by the demodulator's oscillator with an amplitude of 1 (at lower frequencies; higher frequencies will be attenuated). The maximum possible frequency is limited by the demodulator sampling rate and bandwidth; use demodulator order 1 for the least attenuation in demodulator output. This signal may be used with the auxiliary outputs, PID and Threshold Unit for advanced measurement and control tasks. When the demodulator output is written to an auxiliary output, the resulting signal can also be used as a second output channel (for low frequencies).

/dev0/mods/0/carrier/order.Description: Selects the filter roll off between 6 dB/oct and 48 dB/oct for carrier demodulation

/dev0/mods/0/carrier/oscselect.Description: Select the oscillator for the carrier signal.

/dev0/mods/0/carrier/phaseadjust.Description: Adjust the carrier demodulator phase automatically in order to read 0 degrees.

/dev0/mods/0/carrier/phaseshift.Description: Phase shift applied to the reference input of the carrier demodulator and also to the carrier signal on the Signal Outputs

/dev0/mods/0/carrier/timeconstant.Description: Sets the integration time constant or in other words, the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter for the carrier demodulation.

/dev0/mods/0/freqdevenable.Description: In FM mode, choose to work with either modulation index or peak deviation. The modulation index equals peak deviation divided by modulation frequency.

/dev0/mods/0/index.Description: FM modulation index: The modulation index equals peak deviation divided by modulation frequency.

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/amplitude.Description: Set the amplitude of the sideband components.

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/enable.Description: Enable the signal generation for the respective sideband

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/harmonic.Description: Set harmonic of the sideband frequencies. 1 = fundamental

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/inputselect.Description: Select Signal Input for the sideband demodulation

Options.174: "demod_constant_input": Demodulate a constant input. This results in a sine wave of the frequency specified by the demodulator's oscillator with an amplitude of 1 (at lower frequencies; higher frequencies will be attenuated). The maximum possible frequency is limited by the demodulator sampling rate and bandwidth; use demodulator order 1 for the least attenuation in demodulator output. This signal may be used with the auxiliary outputs, PID and Threshold Unit for advanced measurement and control tasks. When the demodulator output is written to an auxiliary output, the resulting signal can also be used as a second output channel (for low frequencies).

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/mode.Description: Enabling of the first sideband and selection of the position of the sideband relative to the carrier frequency for manual mode.

Options.0: "off": Off: First sideband is disabled. The sideband demodulator behaves like a normal demodulator.
Options.1: "upper": C + M: First sideband to the right of the carrier
Options.2: "lower": C - M: First sideband to the left of the carrier

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/order.Description: Selects the filter roll off between 6 dB/oct and 48 dB/oct for sideband demodulation

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/oscselect.Description: Select the oscillator for the second sideband.

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/phaseadjust.Description: Adjust the sideband demodulator phase automatically in order to read 0 degrees.

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/phaseshift.Description: Phase shift applied to the reference input of the sideband demodulator and also to the sideband signal on the Signal Outputs

/dev0/mods/0/sidebands/0/timeconstant.Description: Sets the integration time constant or in other words, the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter for the sideband demodulation.

/dev0/pids/0/center.Description: Sets the center value for the PID output. After adding the Center value, the signal is clamped to Center + Lower Limit and Center + Upper Limit.

/dev0/pids/0/demod/adcselect.Description: Indicates the signal source which is connected to the chosen input demodulator channel.

Options.0: "sigin0", "signal_input0": Signal Input 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.1: "currin0", "current_input0": Current Input 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.2: "trigin0", "trigger_input0": Trigger Input 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.3: "trigin1", "trigger_input1": Trigger Input 2 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.4: "auxout0", "auxiliary_output0": Auxiliary Output 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.5: "auxout1", "auxiliary_output1": Auxiliary Output 2 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.6: "auxout2", "auxiliary_output2": Auxiliary Output 3 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.7: "auxout3", "auxiliary_output3": Auxiliary Output 4 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.8: "auxin0", "auxiliary_input0": Auxiliary Input 1 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.9: "auxin1", "auxiliary_input1": Auxiliary Input 2 is connected to the corresponding demodulator.
Options.174: "demod_constant_input": Constant is connected to the corresponding demodulator. This results in a sine wave of the frequency specified by the demodulator's oscillator with an amplitude of 1 or lower, depending on frequency and filter settings.

/dev0/pids/0/demod/harmonic.Description: Multiplier of the for the reference frequency of the current demodulator.

/dev0/pids/0/demod/order.Description: Selects the filter roll off between 6 dB/oct and 48 dB/oct of the current demodulator.

/dev0/pids/0/demod/timeconstant.Description: Defines the characteristic time constant (cut off) of the demodulator filter used as an input.

/dev0/pids/0/dlimittimeconstant.Description: The cutoff of the low-pass filter for the D limitation given as time constant. When set to 0, the low-pass filter is disabled.

/dev0/pids/0/input.Description: Select input source of PID controller.

/dev0/pids/0/inputchannel.Description: Select input channel of PID controller.

/dev0/pids/0/keepint.Description: If enabled, the accumulated integral error is maintained upon restart of the PID. If is disabled, the integral error is set to zero when the PID is disabled.

/dev0/pids/0/limitlower.Description: Sets the lower limit for the PID output. After adding the Center value, the signal is clamped to Center + Lower Limit and Center + Upper Limit.

/dev0/pids/0/limitupper.Description: Sets the upper limit for the PID output. After adding the Center value, the signal is clamped to Center + Lower Limit and Center + Upper Limit.

/dev0/pids/0/mode.Description: Sets the operation mode of the PID module.

/dev0/pids/0/output.Description: Select output of the PID controller.

Options.2: "oscillator_frequency": Controlling any of the internal oscillator frequencies
Options.3: "demod_phase": Controlling any of the demodulator phase set points
Options.5: "auxout_offset", "auxiliary_output_offset": Driving any of the 4 Auxiliary Outputs' offset
Options.7: "sigout_offset", "signal_output_offset": Driving the main Signal Output's offset

/dev0/pids/0/outputchannel.Description: Select the output channel of the driven output of PID controller.

/dev0/pids/0/phaseunwrap.Description: Enables the phase unwrapping to track phase errors past the +/-180 degree boundary and increase PLL bandwidth.

/dev0/pids/0/pll/automode.Description: This defines the type of automatic adaptation of parameters in the PID.

Options.1: "pid_coeffs": The PID coefficients are automatically set based on the filter parameters.
Options.2: "pid_coeffs_filter_low_bw": The PID coefficients, the filter bandwidth and the output limits are automatically set using a low bandwidth.
Options.3: "pid_coeffs_filter_high_bw": The PID coefficients, the filter bandwidth and the output limits are automatically set using a high bandwidth.

/dev0/pids/0/pll/locked.Description: Indicates when the PID, configured as PLL, is locked.

/dev0/pids/0/rate.Description: PID sampling rate and update rate of PID outputs. Needs to be set substantially higher than the targeted loop filter bandwidth.

/dev0/pids/0/relock/enable.Description: Enable the relock functionality of the PID controller.

/dev0/pids/0/relock/resetintegrator.Description: Enable the reset of integrated error when the trigger event occurs.

Options.0: "off": OFF: Reset of integrator is inactive.
Options.1: "on": ON: Reset of integrator is active.

/dev0/pids/0/relock/resetphaseunwrap.Description: Enable the reset of unwrapped phase when the trigger event occurs.

Options.0: "off": OFF: Reset of phase unwrap is inactive.
Options.1: "on": ON: Reset of phase unwrap is active.

Options.0: "level": Level: As long as the trigger source remains high, the relock is triggered.
Options.1: "edge": Edge: As soon as the trigger source changes from low to high (rising edge), the relock is triggered.

/dev0/pids/0/relock/triggersource.Description: Selects the trigger input for the relock functionality.

Options.-1: "pid_output_overload": PID Output Overload: Trigger event occurs when the PID output value reaches the set range (center + lower limit, center + upper limit)

/dev0/pids/0/setpointtoggle/rate.Description: Defines the rate of setpoint toggling. Note that possible values are logarithmically spaced with a factor of 4 between values.

/dev0/pids/0/setpointtoggle/setpoint.Description: Defines the setpoint value used for setpoint toggle.

/dev0/pids/0/shift.Description: Difference between the current output value Out and the Center. Shift = P*Error + I*Int(Error, dt) + D*dError/dt

/dev0/pids/0/stream/effectiverate.Description: Current rate of the PID stream data sent to PC. Defined based on Max Rate.

/dev0/pids/0/stream/error.Description: PID Error = Set point - PID Input.

/dev0/pids/0/stream/overflow.Description: Indicates the streaming fifo overflow state. 0 = OK, 1 = overflow.

/dev0/pids/0/stream/rate.Description: Target Rate for PID output data sent to PC. This value defines the applied decimation for sending data to the PC. It does not affect any other place where PID data are used.

/dev0/pids/0/stream/shift.Description: Gives the difference between the current output value and the center value. Shift = P*Error + I*Int(Error, dt) + D*dError/dt

/dev0/pids/0/stream/value.Description: Gives the current PID output value.

/dev0/pids/0/value.Description: Gives the current PID output value.

/dev0/scopes/0/trigdelay.Description: Trigger position relative to reference. A positive delay results in less data being acquired before the trigger point, a negative delay results in more data being acquired before the trigger point.

/dev0/scopes/0/trigenable.Description: When triggering is enabled scope data are acquired every time the defined trigger condition is met.

Options.1: "on": ON: Trigger based scope shot acquisition

/dev0/scopes/0/trigfalling.Description: When set (1), enables falling edge triggering. This settings is synchronized with the settings done in the /TRIGSLOPE node.

/dev0/scopes/0/triggate/enable.Description: If enabled the trigger will be gated by the trigger gating input signal. This feature requires the DIG option.

/dev0/scopes/0/triggate/inputselect.Description: Select the signal source used for trigger gating if gating is enabled. This feature requires the DIG option.

Options.0: "trigin0_high", "trigger_input0_high": Only trigger if the Trigger Input 1 is at high level.
Options.1: "trigin0_low", "trigger_input0_low": Only trigger if the Trigger Input 1 is at low level.
Options.2: "trigin1_high", "trigger_input1_high": Only trigger if the Trigger Input 2 is at high level.
Options.3: "trigin1_low", "trigger_input1_low": Only trigger if the Trigger Input 2 is at low level.

/dev0/scopes/0/trigholdoff.Description: Defines the time before the trigger is rearmed after a recording event.

/dev0/scopes/0/trigholdoffcount.Description: Defines the trigger event number that will trigger the next recording after a recording event. A value of '1' will start a recording for each trigger event.

Options.1: "number_of_events": Holdoff is defined as number of events.

/dev0/scopes/0/trighysteresis/absolute.Description: Defines the voltage the source signal must deviate from the trigger level before the trigger is rearmed again. Set to 0 to turn it off. The sign is defined by the Edge setting.

/dev0/scopes/0/trighysteresis/mode.Description: Selects the mode to define the hysteresis strength. The relative mode will work best over the full input range as long as the analog input signal does not suffer from excessive noise.

Options.1: "relative": Selects a hysteresis relative to the adjusted full scale signal input range.

/dev0/scopes/0/trighysteresis/relative.Description: Hysteresis relative to the adjusted full scale signal input range. A hysteresis value larger than 1 (100%) is allowed.

/dev0/scopes/0/trigreference.Description: Trigger reference position relative to the acquired data. Default is 50% (0.5) which results in a reference point in the middle of the acquired data.

/dev0/scopes/0/trigrising.Description: When set (1), enables rising edge triggering. This settings is synchronized with the settings done in the /TRIGFALLING node.

/dev0/scopes/0/trigslope.Description: Sets on which slope of the trigger signal the scope should trigger. This setting is synchronized with the settings done in the /TRIGFALLING and /TRIGRISING nodes.

Options.3: "both": Triggers on both the rising and falling edge.

/dev0/scopes/0/trigstate.Description: When 1, indicates that the trigger signal satisfies the conditions of the trigger.

/dev0/sigins/0/ac.Description: Defines the input coupling for the Signal Inputs. AC coupling inserts a high-pass filter.

/dev0/sigins/0/autorange.Description: Automatic adjustment of the Range to approximately two times the maximum signal input amplitude.

/dev0/sigins/0/diff.Description: Switches between single ended (OFF) and differential (ON) measurements.

/dev0/sigins/0/float.Description: Switches the input between floating (ON) and connected to ground (OFF). This setting applies both to the voltage and the current input. It is recommended to discharge the test device before connecting or to enable this setting only after the signal source has been connected to the Signal Input in grounded mode.

/dev0/sigins/0/imp50.Description: Switches between 50 Ohm (ON) and 10 M Ohm (OFF).

/dev0/sigins/0/max.Description: Indicates the maximum normalized voltage measured on this channel. It can be between -1 and 1. To prevent signal clipping and overvoltage, it is advised to keep it between -0.9 and 0.9.

/dev0/sigins/0/min.Description: Indicates the minimum normalized voltage measured on this channel. It can be between -1 and 1. To prevent signal clipping and overvoltage, it is advised to keep it between -0.9 and 0.9.

/dev0/sigins/0/range.Description: Defines the gain of the analog input amplifier. The range should exceed the incoming signal by roughly a factor two including a potential DC offset. The instrument selects the next higher available range relative to a value inserted by the user. A suitable choice of this setting optimizes the accuracy and signal-to-noise ratio by ensuring that the full dynamic range of the input ADC is used.

/dev0/sigins/0/rangestep/trigger.Description: Switches to the next appropriate input range such that the range fits best with the measured input signal amplitude.

/dev0/sigins/0/scaling.Description: Applies the given scaling factor to the input signal.

/dev0/sigouts/0/add.Description: The signal supplied to the Aux Input 1 is added to the signal output. For differential output the added signal is a common mode offset.

/dev0/sigouts/0/amplitudes/0.Description: Sets the peak amplitude that the oscillator assigned to the given demodulation channel contributes to the signal output.

/dev0/sigouts/0/autorange.Description: If enabled, selects the most suited output range automatically.

/dev0/sigouts/0/diff.Description: Switch between single-ended output (OFF) and differential output (ON). In differential mode the signal swing is defined between Signal Output +V / -V.

/dev0/sigouts/0/enables/0.Description: Enables individual output signal amplitude. When the MD option is used, it is possible to generate signals being the linear combination of the available demodulator frequencies.

/dev0/sigouts/0/imp50.Description: Select the load impedance between 50 Ohm and HiZ. The impedance of the output is always 50 Ohm. For a load impedance of 50 Ohm the displayed voltage is half the output voltage to reflect the voltage seen at the load.

/dev0/sigouts/0/max.Description: Indicates the maximum normalized voltage generated on this channel. It can be between -1 and 1. To prevent signal clipping and overvoltage, it is advised to keep it between -0.9 and 0.9.

/dev0/sigouts/0/min.Description: Indicates the minimum normalized voltage generated on this channel. It can be between -1 and 1. To prevent signal clipping and overvoltage, it is advised to keep it between -0.9 and 0.9.

/dev0/sigouts/0/offset.Description: Defines the DC voltage that is added to the dynamic part of the output signal.

/dev0/sigouts/0/on.Description: Enabling/Disabling the Signal Output. Corresponds to the blue LED indicator on the instrument front panel.

/dev0/sigouts/0/over.Description: Indicates that the signal output is overloaded.

/dev0/sigouts/0/range.Description: Sets the output voltage range. The instrument selects the next higher available range.

/dev0/system/compdelay/calibrate.Description: Perform automatic calibration of the input delay compensation.

/dev0/system/compdelay/delays/0.Description: Current values of the compensation delays. 0: Signal Input 0, 1: Signal Input 1, 2: Aux Inputs, 3: Trigger Inputs, 4: Loopbacks

Options.0: "internal": Internal 10 MHz clock is used as the frequency and time base reference.
Options.1: "external": An external 10 MHz clock is used as the frequency and time base reference. Provide a clean and stable 10 MHz reference to the appropriate back panel connector.

/dev0/system/fwlog.Description: Returns log output of the firmware.

/dev0/system/fwlogenable.Description: Enables logging to the fwlog node.

/dev0/system/fwrevision.Description: Revision of the device-internal controller software.

/dev0/system/identify.Description: Setting this node to 1 will cause the device to blink the power led for a few seconds.

Options.0: "lcr": LCR Impedance Measurement: General-purpose settings for measuring components at finite frequency.
Options.1: "dc": DC Impedance Measurement: Settings for measuring resistance at zero frequency.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/cablelength.Description: Length of cables (One way) used in measurement set up.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/internal/al.Description: Indicates whether smoothing can de applied to the device internal compensation data.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/internal/da.Description: Contains the user compensation data in binary form.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/internal/in.Description: Contains general information about the device internal compensation data.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/internal/st.Description: Store the compensation data persistently on the device. The compensation will be loaded automatically on every power-up.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/internal/va.Description: Indicates whether the device internal calibration data is valid (1 = valid, 0 = invalid).

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/user/allows.Description: Indicates whether smoothing can de applied to the user calibration data.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/user/data.Description: Contains the user compensation data in binary form.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/user/info.Description: Contains general information about the user compensation data.

/dev0/system/impedance/calib/user/valid.Description: Indicates whether the user compensation data is valid (1 = valid, 0 = invalid).

/dev0/system/impedance/filter.Description: Switch between application-based or manually configured impedance settings. A parameter set given by an Application mode can be fine-tuned by changing to Advanced mode. Changing back to Application mode will reset the parameters.

Options.0: "application": Application: The impedance settings are adjusted to fit best the selected application.
Options.1: "advanced": Advanced: The impedance settings are manually configured.

/dev0/system/impedance/freqlimit2t/0/fre.Description: Indicates the limit of a frequency range for 2-terminal impedance measurements.

/dev0/system/impedance/freqlimit2t/0/ran.Description: Indicates the minimum input current range that can be used at frequencies at or above the value in the corresponding freq node for 2-terminal impedance measurements.

/dev0/system/impedance/freqlimit4t/0/fre.Description: Indicates the limit of a frequency range for 4-terminal impedance measurements.

/dev0/system/impedance/freqlimit4t/0/ran.Description: Indicates the minimum input current range that can be used at frequencies at or above the value in the corresponding freq node for 4-terminal impedance measurements.

/dev0/system/impedance/precision.Description: Select the Impedance precision and measurement speed by automatically adjusting the filter bandwidth. If the sweeper module is in impedance application mode the precision setting will also control the sweeper measurement speed.

Options.0: "low": Low -> fast settling: Medium accuracy/precision is optimized for fast response.
Options.1: "high": High -> medium settling: High accuracy/precision takes more settling time.
Options.2: "very_high": Very high -> slow settling: Very high accuracy/precision uses long settling time due to very low bandwidth.

/dev0/system/interfacespeed.Description: Speed of the currently active interface (USB only).

/dev0/system/jumbo.Description: Enables jumbo frames (4k) on the TCP/IP interface. This will reduce the load on the PC and is required to achieve maximal throughput. Make sure that jumbo frames (4k) are enabled on the network card as well. If one of the devices on the network is not able to work with jumbo frames, the connection will fail.

/dev0/system/kerneltype.Description: Returns the type of the data server kernel (mdk or hpk).

/dev0/system/nics/0/defaultgateway.Description: Default gateway configuration for the network connection.

/dev0/system/nics/0/defaultip4.Description: IPv4 address of the device to use if static IP is enabled.

/dev0/system/nics/0/defaultmask.Description: IPv4 mask in case of static IP.

/dev0/system/nics/0/jumbo.Description: Stored setting for jumbo frames. Will be applied after reboot.

/dev0/system/nics/0/mac.Description: Current MAC address of the device network interface.

/dev0/system/nics/0/saveip.Description: If written, this action will program the defined static IP address to the device.

/dev0/system/nics/0/static.Description: Enable this flag if the device is used in a network with fixed IP assignment without a DHCP server.

/dev0/system/owner.Description: Returns the current owner of the device (IP).

/dev0/system/porttcp.Description: Returns the current TCP port used for communication to the dataserver.

/dev0/system/portudp.Description: Returns the current UDP port used for communication to the dataserver.

/dev0/system/preset/busy.Description: Indicates if presets are currently loaded.

/dev0/system/preset/default.Description: Indicates the preset which is used as default preset at start-up of the device.

Options.0: "factory": Select factory preset as default preset.
Options.1: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 1 as default preset.
Options.2: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 2 as default preset.
Options.3: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 3 as default preset.
Options.4: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 4 as default preset.
Options.5: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 5 as default preset.
Options.6: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 6 as default preset.

/dev0/system/preset/error.Description: Indicates if the last operation was illegal. Successful: 0, Error: 1.

/dev0/system/preset/index.Description: Select between factory preset or presets stored in internal flash memory.

Options.1: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 1.
Options.2: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 2.
Options.3: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 3.
Options.4: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 4.
Options.5: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 5.
Options.6: Select the preset stored in internal flash memory at position 6.

/dev0/system/preset/records/0/valid.Description: True if a valid preset is stored.

/dev0/system/preset/save.Description: Save the actual setting as preset.

/dev0/system/properties/freqresolution.Description: The number of bits used to represent a frequency.

/dev0/system/properties/freqscaling.Description: The scale factor to use to convert a frequency represented as a freqresolution-bit integer to a floating point value.

/dev0/system/properties/maxfreq.Description: The maximum oscillator frequency that can be set.

/dev0/system/properties/maxtimeconstant.Description: The maximum demodulator time constant that can be set. Only relevant for lock-in amplifiers.

/dev0/system/properties/minfreq.Description: The minimum oscillator frequency that can be set.

/dev0/system/properties/mintimeconstant.Description: The minimum demodulator time constant that can be set. Only relevant for lock-in amplifiers.

/dev0/system/properties/negativefreq.Description: Indicates whether negative frequencies are supported.

/dev0/system/saveports.Description: Flag indicating that the TCP and UDP ports should be saved.

/dev0/system/shutdown.Description: Sending a '1' to this node initiates a shutdown of the operating system on the device. It is recommended to trigger this shutdown before switching the device off with the hardware switch at the back side of the device.

/dev0/system/stall.Description: Indicates if the network connection is stalled.

/dev0/system/update/labone/data.Description: Node which accepts the Binary file to update the device.

/dev0/system/update/labone/error.Description: An error occurred during the update.

/dev0/system/update/labone/progress.Description: A value between 0 and 1 indicating the update progress.

/dev0/system/update/labone/start.Description: If set to 1 the device starts the update.

/dev0/triggers/in/0/autothreshold.Description: Automatically adjust the trigger threshold. The level is set to fall in the center of the applied transitions.

/dev0/triggers/in/0/level.Description: Trigger voltage level at which the trigger input toggles between low and high. Use 50% amplitude for digital input and consider the trigger hysteresis.

/dev0/triggers/out/0/pulsewidth.Description: Defines the minimal pulse width for the case of Scope events written to the trigger outputs of the device.

/dev0/triggers/out/0/source.Description: Select the signal assigned to the trigger output.

Options.1: "demod1_phase": Oscillator phase of demod 2 (trigger output channel 1) or demod 4 (trigger output channel 2).
Options.2: "scope_trigger": Scope Trigger. Requires the DIG Option.
Options.4: "scope_armed": Scope Armed. Requires the DIG Option.
Options.6: "scope_active": Scope Active. Requires the DIG Option.

/dev0/tu/logicunits/0/inputs/0/channel.Description: Selects threshold channel to be used as input.

/dev0/tu/logicunits/0/internalvalue.Description: Show the value after logical combination but before output settings. The value integrated over some time. Values are 1: low, 2: high, 3: was low and high in the period.

/dev0/tu/logicunits/0/invert.Description: Changes the output signal to low-active.

/dev0/tu/logicunits/0/keep.Description: Hold the output state indefinitely once it has changed to the activated state.

/dev0/tu/logicunits/0/ops/0/value.Description: Logical operation applied to the signals to the left and right of the control.

Options.0: "off": No logical operation selected. No additional signals will be used to generate the output.

/dev0/tu/logicunits/0/pulsewidth.Description: Minimum pulse width for the generated output signal. The width of pulses shorter than this time will be extended.

/dev0/tu/logicunits/0/value.Description: Shows the output value of the logic unit. The value integrated over some time. Values are 1: low, 2: high, 3: was low and high in the period.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/activationtime.Description: Minimum duration of threshold violation needed before the output is activated. This can be used as a glitch filter.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/deactivationtime.Description: Minimum duration of threshold compliance needed before the output is deactivated.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/filter/abs.Description: Takes the absolute value of an analog input signal.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/filter/enable.Description: Enables the low-pass filter applied to the analog input signal

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/filter/filteredval.Description: Shows the value after the low-pass filter.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/filter/mode.Description: Selects the analysis mode defining the output signal.

Options.0: "above_upper": Enable if the Signal is above Upper Threshold.
Options.1: "below_lower": Enable if the Signal is below Lower Threshold.
Options.2: "outside_range": Enable if the Signal is outside the range [Lower Threshold, Upper Threshold].
Options.3: "crossing_both_rising": Enable if the Signal crosses Upper Threshold from below Lower Threshold. The difference between Upper an Lower Threshold defines the threshold hysteresis.
Options.4: "crossing_both_falling": Enable if the Signal crosses Lower Threshold from above Upper Threshold. The difference between Upper an Lower Threshold defines the threshold hysteresis.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/filter/sourcesatur.Description: Flag indicating whether the source value is saturated. Values are: 0: not saturated; 1: saturation at lower bound; 2: saturation at upper bound; 3: saturation at both lower and upper bounds.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/filter/thresholdhi.Description: Upper threshold used to generate the output. In Falling Edge mode, this parameter defines the hysteretic behavior as the output state is reset only when the signal crosses Upper Threshold from below.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/filter/thresholdlo.Description: Lower threshold used to generate the output. In Rising Edge mode, this parameter defines the hysteretic behavior as the output state is reset only when the signal crosses Lower Threshold from above.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/filter/timeconstan.Description: Defines the characteristic time constant (cut off) of the low-pass filter applied to the analog input signal.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/input.Description: Select the signal source to be used in the threshold unit.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/inputchannel.Description: Select the channel according to the selected signal source.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/internalvalue.Description: Shows the value after threshold but before minimum time. The value integrated over some time. Values are 1: low, 2: high, 3: was low and high in the period.

/dev0/tu/thresholds/0/value.Description: Shows the threshold value at the threshold output. The value integrated over some time. Values are 1: low, 2: high, 3: was low and high in the period.
